title: The Market and the Jungle
abstract: arXiv:2611.02635v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study how different institutions governing property rights and economic transactions shape occupational choices and welfare. Individuals in our society choose occupations that determine their production and consumption opportunities, anticipating either anonymous, voluntary market exchange supported by public enforcement (the market), or allocations through a random coercive hierarchy (the jungle) without monetary compensation. We establish conditions for occupational equilibria to exist in the market and in the jungle, and compare their performance. At a common occupational profile, the market maximizes aggregate surplus, whereas allocations in the jungle are Pareto efficient with monetary holdings fixed but need not maximize surplus. Endogenous occupational choices introduce an additional source of institutional differences. translated_abstract: 我们研究了不同的产权与经济交易制度如何塑造职业选择和福利。在我们的社会中，个体选择决定其生产和消费机会的职业，并预期其资源配置要么通过由公共执行机构支持的匿名、自愿的市场交换（“市场”）实现，要么通过随机的强制性等级制度进行且不涉及货币补偿（“丛林”）。我们建立了职业均衡在市场和丛林两种制度下存在的条件，并比较了它们的表现。在相同的职业分布下，市场能够使总剩余最大化，而丛林中的分配在货币持有量固定的条件下虽是帕累托有效的，但不一定使剩余最大化。内生的职业选择为制度差异引入了一个额外的来源。我们发现，市场职业均衡在总体上优于丛林职业均衡。
tldr: 本文构建了一个比较“市场”与“丛林”两种制度下职业均衡的理论框架，证明了在存在内生职业选择的条件下，市场职业均衡在总体福利上优于丛林职业均衡。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a theoretical framework comparing occupational equilibria under "market" versus "jungle" institutions, proving that with endogenous occupational choices, the market occupational equilibrium outperforms the jungle occupational equilibrium in aggregate welfare.
